'''Loukas Grafakos''' ([[Greek language|Greek]]: Λουκάς Γραφάκος) is a Greek mathematician working in [[harmonic analysis]]. He earned his Ph.D. from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], in 1989, under the guidance of [[F. Michael Christ|Michael Christ]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=37103}}.</ref> Grafakos is a Curators Distinguished Professor and holds the Mahala and Rose Houchins Distinguished Chair at the [[University of Missouri]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Loukas Grafakos {{!}} Mathematics - Mathematics |url=https://math.missouri.edu/people/faculty/grafakos |access-date=2024-07-21 |website=math.missouri.edu}}</ref>

Grafakos' research interests include [[Fourier analysis]], [[Singular integral|singular integrals]], and [[Calderón–Zygmund lemma|Calderón–Zygmund theory]]. He is well known for his contributions to the area of multilinear harmonic analysis.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Grafakos |first1=Loukas |last2=Torres |first2=Rodolfo H. |title=Multilinear Calderón–Zygmund Theory |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |date=2002 |volume=165 |issue=1 |pages=124–164 |doi=10.1006/aima.2001.2028 |doi-access=free |issn=0001-8708}}</ref> Grafakos has been supported by the [[National Science Foundation]] and was a [[Simons Foundation|Simons Fellow]] in Mathematics during the academic year 2022-2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 Simons Fellows in Mathematics and Theoretical Physics Announced |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2021/02/04/2021-simons-fellows-in-mathematics-and-theoretical-physics-announced/ |publisher=Simons Foundation |access-date=August 10, 2024}}</ref>

His monographs, “Classical Fourier Analysis”,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Grafakos |first=Loukas |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-1-4939-1194-3 |title=Classical Fourier Analysis |date=2014 |publisher=Springer New York |isbn=978-1-4939-1193-6 |series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics |volume=249 |location=New York, NY |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4939-1194-3}}</ref> “Modern Fourier Analysis”,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Grafakos |first=Loukas |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-1-4939-1230-8 |title=Modern Fourier Analysis |date=2014 |publisher=Springer New York |isbn=978-1-4939-1229-2 |series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics |volume=250 |location=New York, NY |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4939-1230-8}}</ref> and “Fundamentals of Fourier Analysis”,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Grafakos |first=Loukas |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-031-56500-7 |title=Fundamentals of Fourier Analysis |date=2024 |publisher=Springer Cham |isbn=978-3-031-56499-4 |series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics |volume=302 |location=Cham, Switzerland |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-56500-7}}</ref> are widely used as references and as textbooks and provide comprehensive treatment of the subject.

He was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]], in the 2025 class of fellows.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2025|title=2025 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=2024-11-01}}</ref>
